P R A C T I C E M AT E R I A L



HVAC
Pop Quizzes
5 quizzes — one per course — 10 multiple-choice questions each, 50 questions total.


     How to use these quizzes
     Take one quiz at a time, closed book. Circle your answer for each question. Every question is tagged with
     the module it tests, so a miss points straight back to what to review.

     Target: 9 / 10 before moving on to the next course. If you score below 9, review the missed modules
     and retake the quiz.

     Answer key is separate. No answers appear after the individual quizzes. All answers are grouped in a
     separate Answer Key section at the very back, after a clear page break, so you can print the quizzes
     without the answers.

Quiz 1 — HVAC System Essentials
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

  Modules Covered
     Introducing Air Conditioning
     Introducing Air Conditioning High Side Components

INTRODUCING AIR CONDITIONING
1. What does vehicle air conditioning mainly do to cabin air?
   A. Heats the air and raises its humidity
   B. Moves heat from inside the cabin to outside the vehicle, cooling and dehumidifying the air
   C. Creates cold air inside the compressor
   D. Removes all oxygen from the cabin
INTRODUCING AIR CONDITIONING
2. In the refrigeration cycle, refrigerant absorbs heat in the cabin and releases heat outside when it:
   A. Stays as a liquid at constant pressure throughout
   B. Evaporates at low pressure in the evaporator, then is compressed and condenses at high pressure in the
   condenser
   C. Freezes in the condenser
   D. Burns in the compressor
INTRODUCING AIR CONDITIONING
3. Why is the change of state of the refrigerant so important to A/C operation?
   A. It changes the colour of the refrigerant
   B. A liquid boiling to vapour absorbs a large amount of heat, and vapour condensing back to liquid releases
   that heat
   C. It makes the refrigerant heavier
   D. It stops the compressor from turning
INTRODUCING AIR CONDITIONING HIGH SIDE COMPONENTS
4. The high side of the system runs from:
   A. The evaporator outlet back to the expansion device
   B. The compressor discharge, through the condenser, to the inlet of the expansion device / orifice
   C. The cabin filter to the blower motor
   D. The radiator to the heater core
INTRODUCING AIR CONDITIONING HIGH SIDE COMPONENTS
5. What is the job of the condenser?
   A. To absorb heat from cabin air
   B. To reject heat to outside air, changing hot high-pressure vapour into high-pressure liquid
   C. To expand the refrigerant and drop its pressure
   D. To store liquid refrigerant for the low side only



Quiz 1 — HVAC System Essentials                                                                         Page 1 of 2
Quiz 1 — continued
INTRODUCING AIR CONDITIONING HIGH SIDE COMPONENTS
6. A blocked condenser airflow (debris, failed fan) will most directly cause:
    A. Low-side pressure to fall to zero at all times
    B. High-side pressure and temperature to rise, with poor cooling
    C. The evaporator to flood with liquid
    D. The compressor clutch air gap to increase
AIR CONDITIONING LOW SIDE COMPONENTS
7. What happens inside the evaporator?
    A. High-pressure liquid is stored
    B. Low-pressure liquid refrigerant boils and absorbs heat from air passing over the fins
    C. Refrigerant is compressed
    D. Refrigerant gives up heat to outside air
AIR CONDITIONING LOW SIDE COMPONENTS
8. Just before the evaporator, the expansion device (TXV or fixed orifice) causes:
    A. A rise in pressure and temperature
    B. A sharp drop in pressure, so the refrigerant entering the evaporator is cold and low-pressure
    C. The refrigerant to become a superheated vapour
    D. The compressor to stop
A I R C O N D I T I O N I N G S E RV I C I N G
9. Before opening any A/C system, refrigerant must be:
    A. Vented to the atmosphere
    B. Recovered into approved equipment, then the system can be opened, repaired, evacuated, and
    recharged by weight
    C. Diluted with water
    D. Mixed with engine oil and drained
A I R C O N D I T I O N I N G S E RV I C I N G
10. Why is a deep vacuum (evacuation) held on an opened system before recharging?
    A. To inflate the hoses
    B. To remove air and boil off moisture, which would otherwise form acids, cause icing, and reduce cooling
    C. To add oil to the compressor
    D. To test the cabin filter

End of Quiz 1. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Quiz 2 — HVAC System Operation
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

   Modules Covered
       HVAC System Sensor Inputs
       HVAC System Controls
       HVAC System Outputs
       Introducing R1234YF

H VA C S Y S T E M S E N S O R I N P U T S
1. Which set is correctly all HVAC sensor inputs?
    A. Blower motor, blend door actuator, compressor clutch
    B. In-car temperature, ambient temperature, evaporator temperature, sun load, and refrigerant pressure
    sensors
    C. Radiator fan, heater valve, recirculation flap motor
    D. Windshield washer level and fuel level
H VA C S Y S T E M S E N S O R I N P U T S
2. The evaporator temperature sensor is used mainly to:
    A. Measure engine coolant temperature
    B. Prevent evaporator icing by cycling or controlling the compressor before the evaporator freezes
    C. Lock the doors automatically
    D. Measure road speed
H VA C S Y S T E M S E N S O R I N P U T S
3. A faulty refrigerant pressure sensor signal can cause the HVAC module to:
    A. Increase tire pressure
    B. Inhibit compressor engagement if pressure reads too high or too low, to protect the system
    C. Turn off the headlights only
    D. Open the thermostat
H VA C S Y S T E M C O N T R O L S
4. In automatic climate control, the HVAC control module decides blower speed, air distribution, and
temperature by:
    A. Guessing randomly each time the engine starts
    B. Combining the set temperature with sensor inputs and then driving the outputs to reach and hold that
    temperature
    C. Following only the position of the blower switch
    D. Turning every output fully on at all times
H VA C S Y S T E M C O N T R O L S
5. Selecting recirculation instead of fresh air helps most when:
    A. Maximum cooling is needed on a very hot day or outside air is smoky/dirty, because cabin air is reused
    B. The windshield needs demisting in wet weather
    C. The engine is cold and needs warming
    D. The vehicle is being pressure washed

Quiz 2 — HVAC System Operation                                                                           Page 1 of 2
Quiz 2 — continued
H VA C S Y S T E M C O N T R O L S
6. A blend (temperature) door that does not respond to a temperature change request is a fault in which
part of the control loop?
    A. Only the refrigerant charge
    B. The link between the control decision and the output - the blend door actuator, its circuit, or the door itself
    C. The condenser fan only
    D. The sun load sensor lens colour
H VA C S Y S T E M O U T P U T S
7. Which of these is an HVAC output controlled by the module?
    A. Ambient temperature sensor
    B. Blower motor speed, mode/blend door actuators, and compressor clutch or variable compressor control
    C. Refrigerant pressure sensor
    D. Sun load sensor
H VA C S Y S T E M O U T P U T S
8. On a variable-displacement compressor with no clutch, cooling output is varied by:
    A. Removing the drive belt
    B. A control valve/solenoid that changes compressor displacement in response to module command
    C. The cabin filter
    D. Changing tire size
INTRODUCING R1234YF
9. R1234YF was introduced mainly as a replacement for R134a because it has:
    A. Much higher global warming potential
    B. A much lower global warming potential, while working at similar pressures
    C. No need for any oil
    D. A completely different refrigeration cycle with no condenser
INTRODUCING R1234YF
10. Which servicing point about R1234YF is correct?
    A. It can be freely mixed with R134a in any system
    B. It is mildly flammable (A2L), uses its own service fittings and dedicated recovery/recharge equipment,
    and must not be mixed with R134a
    C. It needs no leak testing
    D. Any R134a machine can be used with no changes

End of Quiz 2. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Quiz 3 — HVAC Best Practice Servicing
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

   Modules Covered
       HVAC Performance Checking

H VA C P E R F O R M A N C E C H E C K I N G
1. A correct performance check starts by:
    A. Immediately adding refrigerant
    B. Setting the controls as specified (usually max/cold A/C, recirculation, set blower and engine RPM), noting
    ambient temperature and humidity, and letting pressures and vent temperature stabilise
    C. Removing the condenser fan
    D. Driving at motorway speed with the windows open
H VA C P E R F O R M A N C E C H E C K I N G
2. Centre vent temperature is measured best with:
    A. An infrared gun pointed at the dashboard plastic
    B. A probe thermometer inserted in the centre vent, compared with the specified value for the ambient
    temperature
    C. A finger held in front of the vent
    D. The engine coolant gauge
H VA C P E R F O R M A N C E C H E C K I N G
3. Vent temperature is warmer than specified but both gauge pressures are near normal. A good next
check is:
    A. Condemn the compressor at once
    B. Check for a blend door not reaching full cold, heater valve/heater bleed-through, or a restricted cabin
    filter/airflow fault
    C. Add double the specified charge
    D. Replace the condenser without testing
H VA C P E R F O R M A N C E C H E C K I N G
4. Why must ambient temperature and humidity be recorded during a performance check?
    A. They change the colour of the gauges
    B. Expected vent temperature and pressures rise with ambient heat and humidity, so a reading can only be
    judged against its conditions
    C. They determine the engine oil grade
    D. They have no effect on A/C performance
H VA C P E R F O R M A N C E C H E C K I N G
5. During the check, the condenser fan does not run with A/C on. The likely effect on the readings is:
    A. Lower high-side pressure and colder vent air
    B. Higher high-side pressure and warmer vent air, especially at idle
    C. No change at any speed
    D. Low-side pressure only, with no other change


Quiz 3 — HVAC Best Practice Servicing                                                                    Page 1 of 2
Quiz 3 — continued
H VA C P E R F O R M A N C E C H E C K I N G
6. A system passes the vent-temperature check at fast idle but is poor in slow traffic. This pattern most
suggests:
    A. A fault that appears only under load - check condenser airflow/fan operation and air in the system
    B. The system is fully normal and needs no checks
    C. The cabin filter is new
    D. The refrigerant is overcharged with oil only
H VA C P E R F O R M A N C E C H E C K I N G
7. Touch/temperature checks along the lines during a performance test can help locate:
    A. A radio fault
    B. A restriction - a sharp temperature drop or frosting at one point where there should not be one
    C. Low tire pressure
    D. A worn wheel bearing
H VA C P E R F O R M A N C E C H E C K I N G
8. After a repair, the correct way to confirm the fix is to:
    A. Ask the customer to test it over the next month
    B. Repeat the full performance check under the same conditions and confirm vent temperature and
    pressures are now within specification
    C. Only check that the clutch engages
    D. Clear the fault codes and release the vehicle
H VA C P E R F O R M A N C E C H E C K I N G
9. Superheat/subcooling or line temperatures well outside the expected range during a check most
likely indicate:
    A. A fault with charge level or a component/restriction in the refrigeration loop - investigate before re-gassing
    by guesswork
    B. That the thermometer battery is flat in all cases
    C. A fault in the audio system
    D. That performance checking is not needed
H VA C P E R F O R M A N C E C H E C K I N G
10. A very cold suction line with frost back to the compressor during the check can indicate:
    A. Normal operation on every system
    B. Overfeeding / expansion device stuck open or incorrect charge, risking liquid returning to the compressor
    C. A blocked condenser
    D. A flat battery

End of Quiz 3. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Quiz 4 — HVAC Mechanical Diagnostics
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

  Modules Covered
     Air Conditioning System Pressure Diagnostics
     Air Conditioning Compressor Clutch Diagnostics

AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM PRESSURE DIAGNOSTICS
1. With the system running, BOTH low-side and high-side pressures are lower than normal and cooling
is poor. The most likely cause is:
   A. Overcharge
   B. Undercharge (low refrigerant, often from a leak)
   C. A blocked condenser
   D. Air in the system
AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM PRESSURE DIAGNOSTICS
2. Both pressures are HIGHER than normal with poor cooling on a hot day. Which cause fits best?
   A. Undercharge
   B. Overcharge, air in the system, or poor condenser airflow/cooling
   C. A completely empty system
   D. A failed evaporator blower only
AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM PRESSURE DIAGNOSTICS
3. Low-side pressure is very low (near vacuum) while high-side is low/normal and the evaporator outlet
is cold at one spot. This points to:
   A. A restriction in the low side / metering device or a moisture-iced expansion device
   B. An overcharge
   C. A slipping clutch only
   D. A faulty sun load sensor
AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM PRESSURE DIAGNOSTICS
4. High-side pressure is very high but low-side is near normal, with the liquid line hot. A likely cause is:
   A. A restriction on the high side, such as a blocked condenser or kinked liquid line
   B. A system with no compressor drive
   C. A blown cabin fuse
   D. A worn blower resistor
AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM PRESSURE DIAGNOSTICS
5. Static (engine off, system equalised) pressure is far below the value expected for the ambient
temperature. That tells you:
   A. The compressor is faulty
   B. There is little or no refrigerant charge - leak-test before any running tests
   C. The TXV is stuck open
   D. The clutch gap is too wide




Quiz 4 — HVAC Mechanical Diagnostics                                                               Page 1 of 2
Quiz 4 — continued
AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR CLUTCH DIAGNOSTICS
6. The compressor clutch will not engage. Before condemning the clutch coil, first confirm:
   A. The tire pressures
   B. That the module is commanding engagement and that power and ground actually reach the clutch
   connector
   C. The radio volume
   D. The cabin filter condition
AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR CLUTCH DIAGNOSTICS
7. Power and ground are present at the clutch, but it still does not pull in. Measuring the coil shows an
open circuit. The diagnosis is:
   A. A faulty condenser fan
   B. A failed (open) clutch coil - replace the coil/clutch assembly as specified
   C. Low refrigerant charge
   D. A blocked receiver drier
AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR CLUTCH DIAGNOSTICS
8. The clutch engages but slips, squeals, and gets hot, with a burnt face. A common mechanical cause
to check is:
   A. Excessive clutch air gap, a worn/contaminated clutch face, or a partially seizing compressor raising the
   load
   B. Too much refrigerant oil in the cabin
   C. A new drive belt
   D. High blower speed
AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR CLUTCH DIAGNOSTICS
9. What does the clutch air gap measurement check?
   A. The distance between the condenser and radiator
   B. The gap between the clutch plate and pulley - too wide weakens magnetic pull-in, too narrow can cause
   drag when disengaged
   C. The gap in the spark plugs
   D. The evaporator fin spacing
AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR CLUTCH DIAGNOSTICS
10. The clutch cycles on and off very rapidly (short-cycling). Which checks belong in the diagnosis?
   A. Only the clutch relay paint colour
   B. Refrigerant charge / pressure readings and the evaporator temperature and pressure switch/sensor
   signals that command cycling
   C. Wiper blade size
   D. Wheel alignment

End of Quiz 4. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Quiz 5 — HVAC Electrical Diagnostics
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

   Modules Covered
       Air Conditioning Thermal Mistore Diagnostics
       Sun Load Sensor Voltage Low
       Sun Load Sensor Voltage High

A I R C O N D I T I O N I N G T H E R M A L M I S TO R E D I A G N O S T I C S
1. An air conditioning thermistor (thermal mistore) is:
    A. A fixed resistor that never changes value
    B. A temperature-sensitive resistor whose resistance changes in a known way with temperature, used to
    sense evaporator or cabin air temperature
    C. A type of compressor clutch
    D. A pressure switch with two fixed contacts
A I R C O N D I T I O N I N G T H E R M A L M I S TO R E D I A G N O S T I C S
2. Most automotive temperature thermistors are NTC type. NTC means that as temperature rises:
    A. Resistance rises sharply
    B. Resistance falls
    C. Resistance stays exactly the same
    D. The sensor produces its own voltage like a battery
A I R C O N D I T I O N I N G T H E R M A L M I S TO R E D I A G N O S T I C S
3. An evaporator thermistor reads open circuit. The HVAC module will most likely interpret this as:
    A. An extremely cold or extremely warm evaporator (depending on circuit design) and may inhibit or mis-
    control the compressor - compare scan temperature with actual measured temperature
    B. A correct reading needing no action
    C. Low refrigerant pressure
    D. A condenser fan fault
A I R C O N D I T I O N I N G T H E R M A L M I S TO R E D I A G N O S T I C S
4. To test a thermistor properly, you should:
    A. Only check that its connector is plugged in
    B. Measure its resistance at a known temperature (or compare scan-tool temperature with a thermometer at
    the sensor) and check it changes smoothly as temperature changes
    C. Apply battery voltage directly across it
    D. Short it to ground and watch for sparks
S U N L O A D S E N S O R V O LTA G E L O W
5. A 'sun load sensor voltage low' fault means the module sees the signal:
    A. Above its 5V reference at all times
    B. Below the expected minimum - near 0V - suggesting a short to ground in the signal wire, a failed sensor
    pulling the signal down, or a lost reference/ground fault, depending on circuit design
    C. Exactly at the correct value for bright sun
    D. Only when the headlights are on

Quiz 5 — HVAC Electrical Diagnostics                                                                  Page 1 of 2
Quiz 5 — continued
S U N L O A D S E N S O R V O LTA G E L O W
6. The sun load sensor's normal job is to:
    A. Measure refrigerant pressure
    B. Measure sunlight intensity on the cabin so automatic climate control can add cooling for the side/load the
    sun is heating
    C. Measure vehicle speed
    D. Sense rain on the windshield
S U N L O A D S E N S O R V O LTA G E L O W
7. With the sensor unplugged, the signal wire measures a good reference voltage and ground is good,
but plugged in the signal collapses to near 0V. This points to:
    A. A faulty sensor itself shorting the signal internally
    B. An open signal wire
    C. A faulty blower motor
    D. Low refrigerant charge
S U N L O A D S E N S O R V O LTA G E H I G H
8. A 'sun load sensor voltage high' fault means the module sees the signal:
    A. Stuck at the value for total darkness and correct
    B. At or near the reference voltage / above the expected maximum - suggesting an open signal or ground
    circuit, an unplugged sensor, or a short to voltage
    C. Below 0.2V at all times
    D. Only on cloudy days
S U N L O A D S E N S O R V O LTA G E H I G H
9. A sun load sensor is unplugged during other work and the A/C is then tested. The most likely result
is:
    A. No fault of any kind
    B. A voltage high fault may set, and automatic climate loses sun compensation until the sensor is
    reconnected and the code cleared/retested
    C. The compressor will seize
    D. The evaporator will freeze solid immediately
S U N L O A D S E N S O R V O LTA G E H I G H
10. To distinguish a wiring fault from a sensor fault on a voltage-high code, the best test is:
    A. Replace the HVAC module first
    B. Check the signal, reference, and ground at the sensor connector, then test/replace the sensor only if
    wiring values are correct, and confirm the live signal changes when the sensor is covered and uncovered
    C. Add refrigerant
    D. Replace the compressor clutch

End of Quiz 5. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

                                          Answer Key

HVAC Pop Quizzes — Answer Key                                                                         Divider
Answer Key — Quiz 1: HVAC System Essentials

Retake date: ________________       Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — A/C transfers heat out of the cabin; evaporator cooling also condenses moisture from the air.

2. B — Low-pressure evaporation absorbs heat; compression and high-pressure condensation reject it outside.

3. B — Latent heat in boiling/condensing moves far more heat than temperature change alone.

4. B — The high side is the high-pressure, hot section: compressor outlet to metering device inlet.

5. B — The condenser cools the discharge vapour so it condenses, giving up its heat to outside air.

6. B — If the condenser cannot reject heat, pressure and temperature climb and cooling suffers.

7. B — The evaporator is where cold low-pressure refrigerant evaporates and cools cabin air.

8. B — Metering the liquid creates the pressure drop that makes the evaporator cold.

9. B — Refrigerant is recovered, never vented; recharge is by the specified weight after evacuation.

10. B — Evacuation removes non-condensables and moisture that harm performance and components.




Answer Key — Quiz 1                                                                            Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 2: HVAC System Operation

Retake date: ________________        Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — Sensors report temperatures, sun load, and pressure to the HVAC module; motors and clutches are
outputs.

2. B — If the evaporator gets too cold, frost blocks airflow; its sensor lets the module prevent freeze-up.

3. B — Out-of-range pressure readings lead the module to disable the compressor for protection.

4. B — Automatic control compares target vs. measured conditions and adjusts outputs continuously.

5. A — Recirculating already-cooled cabin air speeds pull-down; fresh air is better for demisting.

6. B — The module may command correctly, but a failed actuator/circuit/door prevents the output moving.

7. B — Blower, doors, and compressor control are driven outputs; sensors are inputs.

8. B — Clutchless compressors vary stroke/displacement electrically instead of cycling a clutch.

9. B — R1234yf has very low GWP compared with R134a and similar operating characteristics.

10. B — R1234yf is A2L mildly flammable, has distinct fittings, and requires dedicated equipment and
procedures.




Answer Key — Quiz 2                                                                              Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 3: HVAC Best Practice Servicing

Retake date: ________________       Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — Comparable results need the manufacturer's test conditions and stabilised readings.

2. B — A probe in the vent airstream, judged against the ambient-based spec, is the reliable check.

3. B — Near-normal pressures point away from the refrigeration loop toward air-side and door faults.

4. B — A vent temp that is normal at 35C ambient would be poor at 20C; conditions set the expectation.

5. B — Without condenser airflow at idle, heat rejection falls, head pressure rises, and cooling drops.

6. A — Speed-dependent cooling points to airflow over the condenser, which road speed provides but traffic
does not.

7. B — An unexpected cold spot or frost marks a restriction creating a pressure drop.

8. B — Repeating the standardised check proves the repair restored specified performance.

9. A — Abnormal superheat/subcooling points to charge or loop faults that gauges and temps together help
isolate.

10. B — Frost to the compressor risks liquid slugging; metering device and charge must be checked.




Answer Key — Quiz 3                                                                             Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 4: HVAC Mechanical Diagnostics

Retake date: ________________        Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — Low charge starves both sides; find and repair the leak, then recharge by weight.

2. B — Excess charge, non-condensables, or poor heat rejection all drive both pressures up.

3. A — Starved evaporator flow pulls suction down; a restriction or icing metering device is likely.

4. A — A high-side blockage backs pressure up ahead of it while the low side can still look near normal.

5. B — Equalised static pressure vs. ambient reveals a low/empty system before the engine is started.

6. B — Many no-engage faults are missing command, feed, or ground - not a failed coil.

7. B — Feed and ground proven good plus an open coil confirms the coil itself has failed.

8. A — Wide gap, worn faces, and high compressor torque all make the clutch slip and overheat.

9. B — Air gap must be in specification for reliable engagement without dragging.

10. B — Short-cycling is usually commanded in response to pressure or evaporator temperature signals, or low
charge.




Answer Key — Quiz 4                                                                              Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 5: HVAC Electrical Diagnostics

Retake date: ________________           Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — Thermistors convert temperature into a resistance/voltage signal the module can read.

2. B — Negative Temperature Coefficient: hotter = lower resistance, which the module reads as a rising signal
voltage in a typical pull-up circuit.

3. A — An open sensor drives the signal to one extreme; live data vs. actual temperature exposes the fault.

4. B — Resistance-at-temperature against the spec chart, plus a smooth change, proves or condemns the
sensor.

5. B — Voltage low codes set when the signal sits below the plausible window, typically a short to ground or
sensor failure.

6. B — Sun load lets auto climate compensate for solar heating before cabin temperature drifts.

7. A — Feed and ground proven good unplugged, signal pulled down when connected, implicates the sensor.

8. B — Voltage high codes set when the signal is pulled up toward reference by an open/short-to-voltage fault.

9. B — An open connector is a classic voltage-high cause; restore the connection and retest the live signal in
light and shade.

10. B — Prove the three wires first; a good sensor signal must vary between covered (dark) and bright light.

End of Answer Key. Practice Material — HVAC Pop Quizzes, 5 quizzes, 50 questions.




Answer Key — Quiz 5                                                                            Separate Key Section
